items.title: Families calling out to loved ones trapped in rubble by Venezuela quakes
items.description: In La Guaira, desperate families keep vigil at buildings where they fear their relatives are trapped, but face an impossible task to move heavy debris.

items.title: In Caracas, this feels like the hardest moment in Venezuela's modern history
items.description: Rescue teams are working ceaselessly to reach those trapped under rubble. But as hope fades, anger is growing.

items.title: US and Iran exchange strikes and accuse each other of violating ceasefire
items.description: Iran says it has launched retaliatory attacks at US infrastructure in Kuwait and Bahrain after the US said it hit multiple targets across Iran.

items.title: Why Kim Jong Un never talks about his mother - or her controversial bloodline
items.description: Very few North Koreans know about her, as her origin could threaten the regime’s legitimacy.

items.title: Israel strikes southern Lebanon as Hezbollah condemns new deal
items.description: Strikes have killed at least one person, state media say a day after Lebanon and Israel signed a framework agreement.

items.title: Heatwave breaks records in Germany, Denmark and Czech Republic
items.description: An estimated 150 million people have been experiencing temperatures of over 35C across Europe.

items.title: Trump's face is added to select US passports for America's 250th birthday
items.description: The commemorative special edition passports will be available on 6 July, and can only be applied for in person

items.title: 117 dead dogs found at California 'no-kill' animal rescue - many with gunshot wounds
items.description: Hundreds more animals are still missing from the California facility as investigators continue excavating the grounds.

items.title: Australia to double maximum penalty for platforms in breach of social media ban
items.description: Children under the age of 16 have been prevented from 10 key social media platforms in Australia since December 2025.

items.title: Budapest's first Pride since Orban left power
items.description: Budapest held its first Pride march since the end of former prime minister Viktor Orban's 16-year government with thousands turning out to celebrate.

items.title: Burkina Faso severs diplomatic ties with France
items.description: The West African country's junta accused the former colonial power of undermining its national interests.

items.title: Religion row as Texas makes Bible stories required reading in schools
items.description: Critics say the new reading requirements infringe on religious freedoms and blur the separation of church and state.
